Base case study  ·  No filters applied  ·  HIT shunt contribution

How the HIT shunt is modelled cancelling harmonic currents

The HIT replaces the distribution transformer and adds an integrated shunt inverter. The shunt path injects equal-and-opposite harmonic currents at the connection node, so only clean fundamental current reaches the grid. This simulation applies no harmonic filters — it measures the HIT shunt contribution in isolation across four architectures. FAIL indicators reflect unfiltered theoretical exceedance, not real facility compliance status.

Without additional filtering, Case 1 still exceeds the limit after HIT — the shunt saturates on six-pulse current alone. This shows a limit of the HIT shunt, not a statement that real Case 1 facilities cannot comply. Cases 1b–3 achieve the reference limit with headroom for voltage regulation and power factor correction.

System: 3 MVA / 480 V LV / 60 Hz ERCOT  ·  ISC/IL = 17.4 (ZT = 5.75%, stiff MV)  ·  Tier < 20  ·  Total Demand Distortion (TDD) limit ≤ 5%  ·  No harmonic filters applied  ·  Reference Design June 2026 v1 DLL (simulated, not field-validated)
Base case: no harmonic filters applied — FAIL badges indicate unfiltered theoretical exceedance, not real facility compliance status. Concurrent services note: this test is harmonics-only at nominal grid. In service, voltage regulation and power factor correction (PFC) share shunt inverter headroom; simultaneous deep sag + heavy harmonic load will reduce cancellation capacity. Case 2 uses measured Eaton 9395P harmonic data (Active Front End (AFE)/12-pulse, 100% load, Phase A avg).
Bar fill shows the measured value; /N% on the right is the IEEE 519-2022 per-order limit for that harmonic. A bar reaching the /N% marker equals the limit exactly.

Assumptions: Cases 1/2/3: three-phase balanced load; ideal six-pulse spectrum (1/h, no commutation overlap or notches). Case 2: Eaton 9395P measured harmonic data (Phase A avg of 3 readings at 100% load; applied uniformly to full rated load). Ideal voltage source (conservative; real Z_T attenuates grid-side injection); full rated load (worst case); ia/ib/ic_comp LP-filtered at 3 kHz (alias rejection, passes h35 at -1.7 dB); sign = -1 (OEM-confirmed shunt cancellation); Hanning Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) (simulation standard; IEC 61000-4-7 required for certified field measurements). Commutation notches not modelled; voltage phenomenon, not cancellable by shunt path. Cooling fractions: 40% (Case 3) is conservative upper bound; 23% (Case 4) from FDDS engineering data (350 kW mechanical cooling per MW IT, PUE 1.5, June 2026).
